[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' appears in the original 1766 religious census return for Derryloran, County Tyrone. In the Drumearn section he is enumerated as ''John Glasco'', immediately after two separate entries for ''Jams Glasco''.<ref>National Archives of Ireland, Parliamentary Return 665, 1766 religious census for Derryloran, ''IHP/1/665'', [https://virtualtreasury.ie/item/NAI-IHP-1-665 original return and transcription], accessed 17 July 2026; independently transcribed in PRONI ''T808/15264''.</ref>

The return concerns householders by religion. It confirms John's residence at Drumearn and places him in a local Glasgow cluster, but gives no age or family relationship. The order of the entries does not establish that either James was his father or brother.

John Glasgow may be connected to [[Glasgow-1343|John Glasgow (abt.1738-)]], though further research is needed to confirm a relationship.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-2988]] is assessed at 22% (uncertain). John is a real Drumearn householder in 1766, following earlier James Glasco occurrences in the local returns. The selected c 1720 James is a feasible father generation and the shared holding context gives a useful local-family hypothesis. Two James households and unrecorded ages leave the exact person and degree open.

Uncertain22%; the c 1750/c 1720 ages are estimates, and householder order or surname repetition is not a parent clause.

Next useful test: Trace the Drumearn holding between the 1740 and 1766 returns for a named successor.

Source basis already held: [https://virtualtreasury.ie/item/NAI-IHP-1-665 National Archives of Ireland, IHP/1/665, 1766 Derryloran religious return; maintained original-return review reused, not newly inspected]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.


=== Drumearn and Martinsburg family review — 17 October 2026 ===

The Geneanet entry already cited in Robert’s saved biography was inspected directly. It represents the man reported born in 1769 in Ireland and dead at Martinsburg on 26 November 1858, with the same wife and children. It explicitly attaches John Glasgow, born 1745 in Ireland, and Margaret, entered under the surname Nee, as parents. John’s own page cites only Ancestry Family Trees. This verifies what the contributed tree says; it does not verify historical paternity, either parent’s birth, or Margaret’s surname. The page gives Ireland, not County Tyrone. Robert’s more specific Tyrone origin remains an inherited local-profile claim.

Select John Glasco of Drumearn (Glasgow-2990) as Robert Glasgow-1189’s possible working father, at 31% subjective confidence. The specific reported father name John favours a John comparison over the automated leading candidate James Glasgow-1970. The actual 1766 Derryloran return places John at Drumearn beside two James Glasco households, three years before Robert’s estimated birth. That supplies a real Tyrone father-generation account compatible with the reported origin. John’s circa-1750 local estimate and the contributed father’s 1745 year are both unproved; either permits fatherhood around 1769, and no date is changed to fit. The estimate assesses the whole proposition that the documented householder was the reported father. It is not a rating of the census record, a statistical probability, or a product of the uncertain ancestry above John.

There are two unresolved steps: whether the contributed John/Margaret parentage is correct, and whether that John was the Drumearn householder. A common given name, estimated generation and claimed county cannot establish identity. The 1766 return supplies no wife, child, age or parent; the nearby James entries do not identify John’s father. Robert’s Tyrone birthplace is not independently established by the inspected Geneanet page. John’s existing uncertain James Glasgow-2988 father is preserved, with no new support. The Cookstown reward subscriber of 1796 is an unresolved namesake comparison, with Robert Glasgow-3941 the stronger maintained candidate; that notice supplies no parent and is not used as proof that the Martinsburg man lived at Cookstown. The single Geneanet/Ancestry family-tree chain and its repetition in WikiTree are not independent witnesses.

Retain another unidentified Irish John as a serious alternative. John Glasgow-3314, associated with Margaret Mill and the West Calder children of 1762–1770, matches both reported parental given names and a viable generation, but has no inspected Robert or Irish-origin bridge. His Scottish baptism and actual West Calder household are distinct facts; an unproved Irish birthplace is not a categorical exclusion. John Glasgow-4179 of Larne also fits the estimated generation; his known Rose Allan marriage does not prove there was no earlier Margaret, but no record connects him with Robert or Drumearn. James Glasgow-1970 has a Cookstown family tradition and a rare Julia/Julia Ann descendant-name resemblance; those are useful regional clues, but do not outweigh the specific reported John father name. If that report is wrong, James or another local man remains possible. No competing candidate is rejected merely for missing fields. No mother is selected: the reported Margaret is not identified with Margaret Mill, Rose Allan or any existing profile, and Nee is not adopted as a verified birth surname. Robert’s wife Elizabeth and every existing child remain unchanged. No merge, vital-field change, live WikiTree save or confidence upgrade is made.

Trace the source of the John/Margaret attachment behind the contributed tree. Inspect the 1803 Caughnawaga baptism and Robert’s American naturalisation, land, probate or family papers for an actual Irish locality or named parent. Compare Drumearn estate/tenancy records and collateral emigrants with the West Calder and Larne alternatives. Keep the eighteenth-century parent question distinct from later descendant record work.

* The 1740 Ulster religious return lists two William and two James Glasgow households at Derryloran, but does not name a child John or state any relationships.<ref>[https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740religiousreturnsulstername.pdf 1740 Religious Returns, Ulster surname transcription], p. 119.</ref> Shared parish and suitable chronology do not identify either William as John's father.
* The two 1766 James entries and John's adjacent entry support a same-townland cluster only. Their relationships remain unproved.

A possible identification concerns John Glasco, charged at Bow Street. John Glasco, Esq., said he was an officer on the Staff and was brought before the Bow Street magistrate charged with wounding patrolman John Smith. The reported incident occurred on Tuesday night after the play in Covent Garden; Glasco was committed.<ref>The Times, 2 May 1799, p.3, Public Office, Bow Street; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/32820363/ record].</ref> Allegation and committal are not conviction. Military status is self-reported and unconfirmed; no Irish origin or kin is stated. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns John Glascow, London chairman. John Glascow, a chairman, said he saw a man in black running with pistols after Martha Ray was shot in Covent Garden.<ref>Derby Mercury, provider-labelled 19 March 1779, p.2; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/394231375/ record]; Old Bailey original, printed p.207; [https://www.dhi.ac.uk/san/ob/1770s/177904040005.gif record]; Old Bailey Proceedings, James Hackman record t17790404-3; event dating only; [https://www.oldbaileyonline.org/record/t17790404-3 record].</ref> The Old Bailey indictment specifies that Martha Ray was shot on 7 April 1779 (printed p.207); that is the event date, not the indictment or newspaper publication date. The newspaper describes evidence after the shooting, not established trial testimony. Its March provider label is incorrect. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow, Loughinsholin freeholder, 1831. The 16 August 1831 declaration lists Robert Glasgow and John Glasgow among freeholders of the barony printed Loughinshollen (modern Loughinsholin), County Londonderry, supporting Sir Robert Bateson. They are co-signatories; no kinship, occupation, age or individual townland is given. Castledawson and 4 July 1831 refer to the opposing meeting discussed in the declaration, not their homes or their signing date.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 16 August 1831, p.3, Loughinshollen freeholders’ declaration; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390548642/ record].</ref> [[Glasgow-2058]], [[Glasgow-3927]] (an indexed freeholder with uncertain locality), [[Glasgow-2990]] and [[Glasgow-4090]] remain adult regional comparisons. No same-name co-signature establishes descent, brotherhood or identity with the Cookstown merchant. The declaration concerns a holding in the barony, not necessarily residence there. The identification remains uncertain.
